hook_text: Long before steel and bricks, South Africans built strong homes from bent sticks, grass and reed mats. How did they stand up?
clip_script: Springbok, Namaqualand. An elder shows us a matjieshuis. First, bendy sticks pushed into the ground in a circle, bent over and tied where they cross. A dome frame, like an upside-down basket. Then reed mats tied on top. Hot day? The reeds shrink and let the breeze in. Rain? They swell and close up. Time to move? Roll the mats, untie the sticks, load them up. Zulu and Xhosa homes use pole frames too, under thick thatch. Struts first, shelter second.
visual_style: Whiteboard framework of bent poles tied into a dome, then covered layer by layer with reed mats or thatch; Nama, Zulu and Xhosa homes side by side.
mood: Proud and respectful, like a heritage day visit.
pacing: Build one frame from the ground up, then three homes and what makes each one clever.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a small dome frame from sticks or straws and string.
